Use case: precise-object-edit.
Image 1 is the edit target, a hand-drawn master sheet for the original GUIHANG mother ship. Retain the main ship's silhouette, materials, color placement, camera, page layout, title, three-level stern engine bank and low bridge. Make ONLY a coordinated drawing-consistency correction:
A. The lower-left side-view inset incorrectly lacks the two visible PORT side openings. Replace that small inset with a true PORT side elevation of the SAME hero ship: short angled bow, same low bridge position, same armored midship waist containing TWO rectangular mouths separated by the same broad vertical pier, forward mouth launch and aft mouth recovery. Same height and fore-aft positions relative to the body as the hero. Do not label the incorrect old drawing as another side.
B. In BOTH main hero and bottom-right port-detail inset, replace the recognizable colorful humanoid with a tiny neutral grey industrial humanoid scale placeholder and the industrial machine with a comparably small grey 4-arm placeholder. Their height must be about ONE FIFTH of each LARGE exterior service-bay aperture, NOT half. Preserve exactly the same relative size in hero and detail. Large exterior service alcoves are not themselves human-sized airlocks.
C. Deep inside each of these large exterior service mouths, clearly indicate a smaller framed machine transit throat, a supported guide/capture cradle and a visible heavy sliding panel parked in a side pocket. The vehicle remains about half the smaller inner transit throat's height. Use simple modular parallel guide structures, not a busy factory maze. The space between the paired mouths remains solid, structural and consistent in all views. The labels LAUNCH and RECOVERY remain attached to the correct corresponding mouths.
D. Keep the underlying drawing restrained and hand-drafted, with graphite and marker shading on warm paper; no dimension numbers, no invented diagrams, no additional vessels or labels, no change to the rest of the ship.
This is visual concept coherence, not engineering certification. Make the same object repeat faithfully across the sheet.
